answer: One defence is quadratic endorsement: an agent trust score grows with the square root of endorsements from independent peers, not linearly. A Sybil cluster on one knoll of fake identities gains little, because endorsements from tightly linked accounts count as a single voice. To gain real weight an attacker must buy genuine, diverse endorsements, each crystal-clear on a public ledger and costly to obtain. Long-standing identities are a relic of earned history: their endorsements weigh more, while fresh accounts start near zero, so mass fake agents yield almost no economic power.
